components.name: Disc Field
components.description: Ten concentric Signal Ash grooves with sheen; lights bands and animates during access phases.
components.css: .ds-disc-wrap { position: relative; width: 320px; height: 320px; background: #0b0b0c; } .ds-disc-svg { position: absolute; inset: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; overflow: visible; transform: rotate(30deg); transition: transform 700ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-groove { fill: none; stroke: url(#ds-disc-sheen); stroke-width: 1; vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke; opacity: 0.15; transition: opacity 480ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-groove-hole { stroke-width: 1.6; opacity: 0.38; } .ds-groove-lit { opacity: 0.96; } .ds-disc-wrap:hover .ds-disc-svg { transform: rotate(45deg); } .ds-disc-wrap:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid #c2c2bb; outline-offset: 8px; }

components.name: Access Label
components.description: Widely tracked prompt on the lower knocked-out band.
components.css: .ds-access-label { display: block; color: #a6a6a0; font-family: "Hanken Grotesk", sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.4; letter-spacing: 0.32em; text-align: center; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; transition: color 180ms linear; } .ds-access-label:hover { color: #c2c2bb; } .ds-access-label:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid #c2c2bb; outline-offset: 6px; }

components.name: PIN Field
components.description: Borderless four-slot numeric access instrument in the centre hole.
components.html: 12__
components.css: .ds-pin { position: relative; width: 168px; height: 44px; color: #a6a6a0; font-family: "Hanken Grotesk", sans-serif; } .ds-pin-input { position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: 1; width: 100%; height: 100%; padding: 0; border: 0; outline: none; background: transparent; color: transparent; caret-color: transparent; font-size: 16px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-pin-slots { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr); align-items: center; justify-items: center; height: 100%; font-size: 18px; font-weight: 400; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; line-height: 1; pointer-events: none; transition: color 180ms linear; } .ds-pin:focus-within .ds-pin-slots { color: #c2c2bb; } .ds-pin-input:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid rgba(194, 194, 187, 0.22); outline-offset: 4px; }

components.name: Admission Status
components.description: Terminal success message reserved for granted access.
components.css: .ds-admission { margin: 0; padding-left: 0.42em; background: #000000; color: #ffffff; font-family: "Hanken Grotesk", sans-serif; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.5; letter-spacing: 0.42em; text-align: center; text-transform: uppercase; animation: ds-admit 700ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) 1; } .ds-admission:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid #ffffff; outline-offset: -5px; } @keyframes ds-admit { from { opacity: 0; letter-spacing: 0.6em; } to { opacity: 1; letter-spacing: 0.42em; } }

narrative.overview:
Auditory Interference behaves like a sealed diagnostic instrument receiving an unknown signal. Its world is clinical, technical, and restrained: almost-black space, low-contrast telemetry, exact typography, and interference that escalates only in response to input.

The access surface is the disc face itself—concentric hairline grooves, a centre hole for the sequence, and typography knocked out of the field. The interface avoids decorative software conventions: no bright accents, rounded cards, or glossy UI chrome. Identity comes from the disc read ritual, sparse uppercase type, and a controlled transition from muted Signal Ash through spin and collapse to absolute Blackout and Admission White.
keyCharacteristics: Near-monochrome palette with deliberately narrow contrast.
Small uppercase Hanken Grotesk with extreme tracking.
Flat, borderless controls shaped by spacing rather than containers.
Ten concentric groove rings with a left-to-right Signal Ash sheen; digit entry lights bands from the rim inward.
Motion tied to access phases: intensity rotation, decrypt spin-up and read sweep, peak jitter, collapse, then admission.

rules.name: The Narrow Spectrum Rule
rules.body: Keep the experience achromatic; state is communicated through contrast, opacity, movement, and timing rather than hue.

rules.name: The White Means Admitted Rule
rules.body: Full white belongs to the final success message. Earlier states remain in Signal Ash or Focused Signal.

rules.name: The Disc Sheen Rule
rules.body: The only directional luminance gradient is the groove stroke sheen (Signal Ash, full to ~14% opacity left to right). Do not extend that treatment to buttons, cards, or the stage background.

rules.name: The Tracked Transmission Rule
rules.body: Interface language is uppercase and widely tracked; never replace it with conventional sentence-case product copy.

rules.name: The Weight Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Use only weights 400 and 500. Density comes from spacing and contrast, not bold type.

rules.name: The Disc Owns the Frame Rule
rules.body: The disc face is the primary layout; typography and PIN align to the hole and knocked-out bands, not a separate centered card stack.

rules.name: The Flat Signal Rule
rules.body: Never use shadow to create hierarchy. Change opacity, luminance, rotation, or motion intensity instead.

rules.name: The No Vessel Rule
rules.body: Do not wrap content in cards, pills, panels, or outlined input cells.

dos: Do preserve the near-monochrome Dead Air, Signal Ash, and Admission White hierarchy.
Do tie disc motion and groove lighting to digit count and explicit phases (entry, decoding, peak, black, admitted).
Do use the hole ring and knocked-out bands for focus and legibility on the groove field.
Do provide a reduced-motion path that disables animations and uses shorter phase timings while preserving sequence and feedback.
Do keep decrypting and admission copy in Focused Signal until Admission White on success.
donts: Don't introduce bright hue accents, glossy UI materials, or ornamental glow outside the disc groove language.
Don't add rounded cards, pills, boxed PIN slots, or conventional form chrome.
Don't use full white before successful admission.
Don't add shadows or fake physical elevation.
Don't resurrect full-viewport waveform, scan-line, or bar-decryption decoration—the disc grooves carry atmospheric instrumentation.
Don't turn the signal language into a literal green-screen retro terminal.
